question: Whether a bounded next Settings acceptance run on isolated macos-15 ARM is an evidence-backed resource strategy without changing thresholds or claiming product behavior.

verdict_A_resource_acceptance.finding: Run 37731576716 package and browser jobs were admitted and resource-valid; the guest was admitted, then became resource-invalid before a Settings case receipt. The run has zero native Settings acceptance credit and all native product verdicts remain unknown.
verdict_A_resource_acceptance.basis: The boundary record reports no settings-case receipt and unverified T34/T64/reload/restoration/downstream consumers. Its retained artifact tree has five files: the three run-matched journals and two screenshots. Its enumerated evidence paths and hashes agree with the retained files; there is no Settings acceptance receipt in the tree.
verdict_A_resource_acceptance.screenshot_limit: A panel-context-ready log and an opening screenshot do not prove that a Settings case step ran.

verdict_B_evidence_quality.finding: The resource comparison supports a host-strategy experiment only. It does not establish that CPU pressure caused a product failure.

The supplied ARM examples are other acceptance workflows; this comparison is resource evidence, not a controlled cross-architecture Settings experiment.
